answer: A useful sybil defense is to make each agent earn influence through a scarce, nontransferable reputation bond: it must lock capital, complete repeated tasks, and risk losing the bond when its work is challenged and found fraudulent. New identities start with little weight, so splitting one stake across many accounts does not multiply influence. The vine of trust grows only through costly history; each delta in reputation reflects verified work. To attack the river of decisions, an adversary must fund many bonds and keep them exposed to slashing.
